-OrRNUkj_zeNh2cscqms.accomplishment: When I moved to the United States from Russia in the fourth grade, animation became my bridge to breaking the language barrier, since talking about indie animation or mainstream anime gave me an easy way to connect with people even without sharing the same background or childhood experiences. In ninth grade, I watched Jin-Roh by Hiroyuki Okiura, and the animation immediately stood out to me because every detail felt deliberate, from the slow, heavy movement of the police armor that communicated weight and control, to the contrast between dark industrial settings and sudden bursts of fire and light. That was the moment I stopped seeing animation as just entertainment and started thinking about how meaning is constructed through movement, timing, and visual choices, which pushed me to start drawing on my own in an attempt to understand how professional animators build emotion and narrative through motion rather than words. Now, as a High Level IB Visual Arts student and through a 2D animation course in a partnership program between the Pratt Institute and my school, I am continuing to develop both my technical skills and my understanding of storytelling. Through that process, I’ve become more consistent in how I approach learning and practice. That consistency is something I can bring to Volta, especially when working with new people, perspectives, and ideas.
